falsification.answer: The outflow is indistinguishable from an authorised treasury, bridge or migration movement: no protocol attribution, no caller or permission evidence, and exposure.integrators is empty, so no loss bearer is demonstrated.

ai.mechanism: Evidence shows only a single transfer emptying 100% of the USDC balance (4,190,629.677573 USDC, ~$4,190,630) from 0x100ae042ef0ea159ecc3513e9a378ff21f3829ba. The packet contains no call trace, no caller/role data, no protocol or instrument attribution and no failed-authorisation signal, so no exploit mechanism can be named.
ai.lossBearer: Unidentified. The drained address 0x100ae042ef0ea159ecc3513e9a378ff21f3829ba is not attributed to any protocol, and the integrator list is empty, so no downstream loss bearer is shown.
ai.narrative: A contract on Ethereum had its entire USDC balance moved out in one transaction: 4,190,629.677573 USDC, about $4,190,630, leaving nothing behind. That full-sweep pattern is what a drain looks like, but it is also exactly what a treasury sweep, a bridge settlement or a migration to a new contract looks like. The packet gives no owner, no protocol name, no caller permissions and no affected integrators, so there is no way to tell an unauthorised withdrawal from a routine one. Nothing here establishes who would actually lose money, so there is no tradeable loss path to act on.
ai.vetoReason: The outflow is indistinguishable from an authorised treasury, bridge or migration movement: no protocol attribution, no caller or permission evidence, and exposure.integrators is empty, so no loss bearer is demonstrated.
concerns: No call trace or caller/role evidence to distinguish authorised from unauthorised withdrawal
Drained address not attributed to any protocol or instrument
Integrator exposure list is empty; no downstream victim identified
Full-balance sweep is consistent with migration or bridge settlement per the packet note

aiDecision.thesis: A single transfer moving 100% of a $4.19M USDC balance out of an unattributed EOA/contract is indistinguishable from a treasury or hot-wallet sweep. No protocol attribution, no call trace, no failed-auth signal, no integrator exposure, and no listed instrument maps to the address, so no causal loss path to any tradable token exists.
aiDecision.invalidation: Attribution of 0x100ae0... to a listed protocol's treasury/vault plus exploit confirmation (trace showing unauthorised caller) would reopen a direct short.
aiDecision.rationale: Investigator veto stands: mechanism unknown, loss bearer unidentified, candidate list empty. Clean full-balance USDC transfers are far more often authorised operations than exploits. With zero candidates there is no instrument that could pay, so sizing is moot; acting would be inventing a market. Monitoring adds nothing without attribution, so decline.
